concepts.quote: the loop only stops after the condition has become true
concepts.why: The loop stops when i < 3 becomes false. At i = 3 the test is false, so the body never prints 3, and the student accepts the wrong trace line.

concepts.quote: Yes, the loop only stops after the condition has become true
concepts.why: A for loop exits when its condition is false, but the student says the trace is right and thinks it stops when the condition becomes true.

concepts.quote: the loop only stops after the condition has become true
concepts.why: This is the listed misconception 'For and while loops end when the condition becomes true'.
The answer says nothing about loops that never end.
